questions: Do you remain fully aware throughout the movements?
Do the movements ever cause you to lose awareness or become unresponsive?
Do the movements continue while you are asleep?
Did the movements begin suddenly?
Have the movements been continuously present since they began?
Can you voluntarily stop or suppress the movements, even briefly?
Do you feel an urge or inner tension before a movement that is relieved after performing it?
Are the movements worse when you are anxious, stressed, or concentrating?
Have you had similar involuntary movements before this illness?
Have you recently started, stopped, or changed the dose of any medication?
Have you recently taken an antipsychotic, anti-nausea medication, antidepressant, stimulant, seizure medication, or medication for Parkinson’s disease?
Have you recently used recreational drugs, excessive alcohol, or suddenly stopped regular alcohol or sedative use?
Do you have a history of liver disease, kidney disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, or electrolyte problems?
Have you recently had a fever or serious infection?
Have you recently had a head injury or stroke-like symptoms?
Do you have weakness, numbness, or loss of coordination on one side of your body?
Have you noticed yellowing of your eyes or skin?
Have you had recent unexplained weight loss, abdominal pain, or changes in your speech or swallowing?
Do close relatives have similar involuntary movements or a diagnosed movement disorder?
Are you pregnant or could you be pregnant?
